The World Association for Christian Communication Africa Region has elected Lekan Otufodunrin of Journalists for Christ International Outreach, Nigeria, as its president for a four-year term. This was contained in a statement signed by Secretary of WACC Africa, Blessing Oladunjoye, on Monday. WACC is a non-governmental, non-profit organisation that promotes communication rights and social justice. WACC advocates inclusive communication and provides guidance and support to people regardless of their religion, ethnicity, gender or culture. Otufodunrin emerged as president at the association’s General Assembly held on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, alongside other executive members elected to lead its Africa Region for the next four years. Other elected officials include Blessing Oladunjoye of the BO Foundation for Inclusive Media, Nigeria, as secretary and Mwendwa Kivuva, a member of the Board of Trustees of the Kenya ICT Action Network, Kenya, as treasurer. George Stewart, a media development specialist from Liberia, and Nigerian journalist Opeyemi Lawal were elected as alternate executive members. Reporter Slam Nigeria targets global journalism glory Reporter’s diary: South Africa through the eyes of MIP 5 fellows CJN pushes responsible AI use in justice system In addition to their regional leadership roles, Otufodunrin and Joof-Cole will serve as members of the WACC UK Board. In his acceptance remarks, Otufodunrin pledged that the new executive would implement programmes to advance the association’s focus on digital justice, gender justice and climate justice across the continent. At the opening ceremony, the convener of the West Africa Digital Rights Defenders Coalition, Kehinde Adegboyega, called for universal digital access, rights safeguards and data sovereignty in Africa. Delivering a keynote address titled Ensuring Digital Justice in Africa, Adegboyega said regional efforts should focus on capacity building, policy advocacy, coalition building and community action. “No digital future is just until it is inclusive, free and grounded in dignity for all Africans,” Adegoyega stated. Also speaking, the Staff Liaison for the WACC Africa Region, Dr Sarah Macharia, commended the outgoing executive, led by Matomklawè Kpalla, for its achievements. She urged the newly elected officials to build on the successes of their predecessors and strengthen the association’s standing across the region. The new executive is expected to serve for four years. Adetutu Sobowale Adetutu has three years experience in publishing stories on gender, health, education, metro and fact-checking.
